skill.name: remotion-to-hyperframes
skill.description: Converts existing Remotion React video compositions into HyperFrames HTML and GSAP timelines, with linting and visual comparison guidance.
skill.summary: Convert Remotion source into HyperFrames HTML with migration rules and validation guidance.
skill.author: heygen-com

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are false positives from Markdown, TypeScript template literals, fixed relative paths, and test fixtures that are parsed but not executed. I confirmed low-risk external network guidance where generated examples load CDN scripts or fonts, and added a semantic medium finding for the optional corpus harness. No prompt injection or credential exfiltration evidence was found.

remediation.issue: The optional corpus harness can install packages and execute render tooling.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user approval before running it, document every external command, and prefer locked installs with lifecycle scripts disabled where possible.

remediation.issue: Reference output may load scripts or fonts from third-party CDNs.
remediation.suggestion: Vendor required browser libraries or add integrity pinning and clear network-use documentation for generated HTML.

remediation.issue: Media comparison scripts process user-supplied video files through ffmpeg tooling.
remediation.suggestion: Keep shell invocation disabled, validate file paths before use, and run comparisons inside a trusted local workspace.

content.value_statement: Teams moving Remotion videos to HyperFrames need clear mapping, blockers, and validation steps. This skill guides source linting, API translation, output structure, and SSIM-based checks.
actual_capabilities: Lints Remotion TS and TSX source for unsupported animation patterns.
Maps common Remotion APIs to HyperFrames HTML and GSAP timeline patterns.
Defines the expected HyperFrames stage, scene, data attribute, and timeline structure.
Provides reference guides for timing, sequencing, media, fonts, Lottie, and parameters.
Includes a tiered test corpus with SSIM thresholds for visual validation.
Explains when to stop translation and recommend runtime interop instead.
limitations: It only supports explicit Remotion to HyperFrames migration requests.
It does not export HyperFrames back to Remotion or other frameworks.
State machines, side effects, async metadata, and third-party UI libraries may block translation.
Validation requires local Node, Remotion, HyperFrames CLI, ffmpeg, and project dependencies.

use_cases.title: Migrate production video templates
use_cases.description: Convert existing Remotion compositions into HyperFrames HTML while preserving timing, scenes, props, and media behavior.

use_cases.title: Guide AI code conversion
use_cases.description: Give Claude, Codex, or Claude Code a structured workflow for translating source and documenting unsupported patterns.

use_cases.title: Validate migration fidelity
use_cases.description: Compare Remotion and HyperFrames renders with SSIM thresholds and frame strips before accepting a translation.

prompt_templates.title: Check a Remotion project
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Remotion source for HyperFrames migration. Identify blockers, warnings, required references, and the safest next step.

prompt_templates.title: Translate one composition
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert this Remotion composition into HyperFrames HTML. Preserve timing, dimensions, props, media paths, and document any translation gaps.

prompt_templates.title: Handle unsupported APIs
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze these lint findings. Explain which patterns block translation, which can be dropped, and what interop path I should use.

prompt_templates.title: Validate visual fidelity
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan and interpret a Remotion versus HyperFrames render comparison. Use the relevant SSIM threshold and identify likely fixes for divergence.

output_examples.input: A Remotion title card with a fade-in text animation.
output_examples.output: A HyperFrames stage with one scene, matching duration metadata, and a GSAP opacity tween for the text.

output_examples.input: A multi-scene Remotion composition using sequences, image media, and spring timing.
output_examples.output: A scene timeline plan that maps each sequence to data attributes and documents the equivalent GSAP timing.

output_examples.input: A Remotion source that uses useState, useEffect, and async metadata.
output_examples.output: A refusal to translate directly, with a recommendation to use runtime interop or resolve data before build time.

best_practices: Run the linter before translation and stop when blocker findings appear.
Load only the reference guides that match APIs used by the source project.
Document dropped constructs, approximations, asset copies, and validation results in translation notes.
anti_patterns: Using this skill for new HyperFrames authoring instead of an explicit Remotion migration.
Ignoring linter blockers and producing HTML that cannot reproduce frame-driven behavior.
Accepting a translation without rendering both versions and comparing visual fidelity.

faq.question: Does this skill create new HyperFrames videos?
faq.answer: No. It is for explicit Remotion source migration. New videos should use a native HyperFrames authoring workflow.

faq.question: Can it convert HyperFrames back to Remotion?
faq.answer: No. The workflow is one way from Remotion source to HyperFrames HTML.

faq.question: What input should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide the Remotion composition source, relevant props, assets, package context, and the desired composition ID.

faq.question: What happens when lint blockers are found?
faq.answer: The skill should stop direct translation and recommend runtime interop or a source rewrite.

faq.question: Does the skill run external tools?
faq.answer: It includes optional scripts for linting, rendering, and SSIM comparison. Review them before running in a trusted local environment.

faq.question: How is translation quality checked?
faq.answer: Render the Remotion baseline and HyperFrames output, then compare frames with the SSIM diff workflow.
